wcag.definition: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines. A set of international standards that explain how to make web content easier to use for people with disabilities.
wcag.simple: Rules that help websites and apps work for everyone, including people who cannot see, hear, or use a mouse.

alt text.definition: Alternative text that describes an image for people who cannot see it.
alt text.simple: A short written description of a picture so screen readers can read it aloud.

screen reader.definition: Software that reads screen content out loud or converts it to braille for blind or low-vision users.
screen reader.simple: A program that reads what is on the screen so blind people can use a computer.

dyslexia.definition: A learning difference that makes reading, spelling, and writing more difficult.
dyslexia.simple: A condition that makes reading and spelling harder for some people.

cognitive disability.definition: A disability that affects thinking, memory, attention, or learning.
cognitive disability.simple: A condition that can make it harder to think, remember, focus, or learn new things.

plain language.definition: Writing that is easy to read and understand the first time.
plain language.simple: Words written in a simple way so most people can understand quickly.

accommodation.definition: A change that helps a person with a disability do their job or access information.
accommodation.simple: A helpful change that makes work or information easier for someone with a disability.

ada.definition: Americans with Disabilities Act. A United States law that protects people with disabilities from discrimination.
ada.simple: A US law that says people with disabilities should have the same chances as everyone else.

section 508.definition: A US federal law requiring government digital tools to be accessible to people with disabilities.
section 508.simple: A rule that says government websites and software must work for people with disabilities.

neurodivergent.definition: People whose brains work differently in ways such as autism, ADHD, or dyslexia.
neurodivergent.simple: People whose brains work differently, like those with autism, ADHD, or dyslexia.

assistive technology.definition: Tools or software that help people with disabilities do everyday tasks.
assistive technology.simple: Tools or apps that help people with disabilities do everyday tasks.

cognitive load.definition: The amount of mental effort needed to understand or complete a task.
cognitive load.simple: How much thinking effort a task takes.

accessible pdf.definition: A PDF document that can be read by screen readers and used by people with disabilities.
accessible pdf.simple: A PDF that screen readers can read and people with disabilities can use.

color contrast.definition: The difference in brightness between text and background, which affects readability.
color contrast.simple: How easy it is to see text against its background.

keyboard navigation.definition: Using a keyboard instead of a mouse to move through a website or app.
keyboard navigation.simple: Moving through a website or app using only the keyboard.

focus indicator.definition: A visible outline that shows which element on the screen is currently selected.
focus indicator.simple: The highlight that shows which button or field is currently selected.

caption.definition: Text that appears on screen with video or audio to show what is being said.
caption.simple: The words shown on screen for videos so deaf or hard-of-hearing people can follow along.

transcript.definition: A written version of spoken audio or video content.
transcript.simple: The written text of what was said in a video or meeting.

universal design.definition: Designing products and spaces so they work for the widest range of people, including those with disabilities.
universal design.simple: Making things that work well for as many people as possible, including people with disabilities.

inclusive design.definition: Designing with the needs of people who are often excluded, such as people with disabilities.
inclusive design.simple: Designing things so that people who are often left out can use them too.

audio description.definition: Spoken narration added to video to describe important visual details for blind viewers.
audio description.simple: Extra spoken explanation in a video that tells blind viewers what is happening visually.

disability disclosure.definition: When a person tells their employer or team that they have a disability.
disability disclosure.simple: When someone tells their team or employer that they have a disability.

reasonable accommodation.definition: A workplace change that helps an employee with a disability do their job, as long as it does not cause major difficulty for the employer.
reasonable accommodation.simple: A workplace change that helps an employee with a disability do their job.

screen magnifier.definition: Software that enlarges part of the screen for people with low vision.
screen magnifier.simple: Software that makes parts of the screen bigger for people with low vision.

voice control.definition: Software that lets someone control a computer or phone by speaking commands.
voice control.simple: Using your voice to control a computer or phone instead of typing or clicking.

closed caption.definition: Captions that can be turned on or off by the viewer.
closed caption.simple: Video subtitles that the viewer can turn on or off.

open caption.definition: Captions that are always visible on the video and cannot be turned off.
open caption.simple: Video subtitles that are always shown and cannot be turned off.
